description: Baseline: loss=ns, dim=200, epoch=75, lr=0.2, wordNgrams=2, minn=2, maxn=6, minCount=1, no oversample. 12 classes, weighted_f1=0.8231, bottom5_mean=0.6169.

asi.hypothesis: Baseline run to establish reference for optimization loop.

description: loss=ova: weighted_f1=0.8220 (-0.0011 vs baseline). Slightly worse overall, bottom5_mean +0.0058. nafar-erdigunea +1.4pp, ekialde-nafarra +0.6pp but zuberera -0.36pp. Small gains on weak classes but not worth 42s slower training.

asi.hypothesis: ova loss (one-vs-all binary CE) should help imbalanced classes
asi.verdict: marginal loss, slows training significantly (+42s), bottom5 improves but overall weighted_f1 drops slightly
asi.next_action_hint: try loss=hs (hierarchical softmax) since classes have natural hierarchy

description: loss=hs: weighted_f1=0.7805 (-0.0426 vs baseline). Catastrophic across weak classes: nafar-hego-sartaldea 0.39, nafar-erdigunea 0.51, naflap-sartaldea 0.48. HS is designed for large output spaces but destroys minority class performance here.

asi.hypothesis: hierarchical softmax helps imbalanced hierarchy
asi.verdict: worse than ns on every metric. HS's tree structure likely puts minority classes deep in the traversal, increasing error propagation
asi.next_action_hint: stick with ns loss, try oversampling to directly address class imbalance instead
asi.rollback_reason: catastrophic -4.3pp weighted_f1, bottom5 drops from 0.62 to 0.48

description: oversample_factor=4: weighted_f1=0.7945 (-0.0286). Oversampling hurt everywhere — even top classes degraded (mendebal-sortaldea 88.4→85.1%, zuberera 95.4→94.3%). Known pattern from prior experiments: flat oversampling collapses accuracy. Need targeted/minimal oversampling.

asi.hypothesis: oversample_factor=4 balances classes more aggressively
asi.verdict: catastrophic loss across the board, confirms flat oversampling is harmful for this dataset. Top classes suffer from noise injection during oversampling of minority classes
asi.next_action_hint: try dim=300 for more model capacity to handle class disparity without oversampling, or try wordNgrams=3 for more contextual signal

description: dim=300: weighted_f1=0.8223 (-0.0008). Identical to dim=200 (0.8231), within noise. Training time doubled (120→197s). More capacity doesn't help the class imbalance problem.

asi.hypothesis: dim=300 gives model more capacity to handle 12-class disparity
asi.verdict: no improvement, within noise. The bottleneck is not model capacity but data quality/quantity for minority classes
asi.next_action_hint: try wordNgrams=3 — trigrams might capture dialectal phrasing better than bigrams, helping distinguish closely-related classes like nafar variants

description: baseline: mendebal-sartaldea data expansion (+167 passages from 19 new towns). F1 stayed flat (~0.823) — new data didn't hurt but also didn't immediately help the Bizkaian confusion.

asi.hypothesis: Adding 19 new mendebal-sartaldea towns (~167 passages, ~100-150 clean sentences) would increase class representation and help distinguish Western Bizkaian from Eastern Bizkaian
asi.result: weighted F1 stayed flat at 0.823 — the new data is small (~7% increase) and may need +epoch or different loss to leverage it

description: wordNgrams=3: weighted_f1=0.8231 vs baseline 0.8230. Trigrams add no value — dialectal markers are already captured at bigram level. Training was actually faster (108s vs 120s).

asi.hypothesis: wordNgrams=3 captures dialectal multi-word phrases better than bigrams
asi.verdict: no improvement, trigrams don't help for these Basque subdialects — n-gram level dialectal markers are short (1-2 words)
asi.next_action_hint: try minCount=2 or minCount=5 to filter noise words that confuse minority classes

description: minCount=2: weighted_f1=0.8225 (-0.0004). Filtering singletons slightly hurts — rare dialectal words carry signal for minority classes.

asi.hypothesis: minCount=2 filters noise words that mislead minority classes
asi.verdict: slightly worse, rare words are dialectal signal not noise for Basque
asi.next_action_hint: try minn=3,maxn=8 for longer morphological subword units

description: minn=3,maxn=8: weighted_f1=0.8207 (-0.0022). Wider char n-gram range hurts — minn=2 is needed for Basque short morphological markers (case endings, verb inflections). zuberera dropped from 0.95 to 0.94.

asi.hypothesis: minn=3,maxn=8 captures longer morphological segments more specific to dialects
asi.verdict: worse, losing minn=2 removes important short Basque morphemes (case markers, aspect suffixes) that carry dialect signal
asi.next_action_hint: try epoch=150,lr=0.1 — longer training with lower LR for better minority class convergence

description: epoch=150,lr=0.1: weighted_f1=0.8221 (-0.0008). Double training time (231s), no improvement. More epochs don't help — model converges at ~75 epochs with current data.

asi.hypothesis: epoch=150,lr=0.1 gives more training time for minority classes to converge
asi.verdict: no improvement, model already converged at epoch=75. Longer training just wastes time. The bottleneck is data scarcity for Nafarroa minorities, not training duration
asi.next_action_hint: try lr=0.05 — very low LR might find better minima for minority classes, or try targeted oversampling on bottom-3 only instead of flat oversampling

description: lr=0.3: weighted_f1=0.8210 (-0.0019). Higher LR slightly worse — 0.2 is the sweet spot for this data size.

asi.hypothesis: lr=0.3 explores more aggressively, helping minority classes escape local minima
asi.verdict: slightly worse, lr=0.2 is optimal. Hyperparameter tuning is exhausted — need architecture change (loss=ova on new data, or two-stage)
asi.next_action_hint: retry loss=ova with the expanded dataset — the class distribution changed, ova might work better now

description: loss=ova on expanded dataset: weighted_f1=0.8226 (-0.0003 vs baseline ns). Still within noise. Ova doesn't outperform ns even with more mendebal-sartaldea data. ns remains the best loss function.

asi.hypothesis: loss=ova with expanded mendebal-sartaldea data might now outperform ns since bottom classes changed
asi.verdict: still within noise of ns baseline. ova is not the solution for this dataset
asi.next_action_hint: keep ns loss, quantize model. Next big move: two-stage classifier architecture

description: targeted oversample factor=4 (bottom-half only): weighted_f1=0.8245 (+0.0016 vs baseline). Bottom classes improved without top class degradation. naflap-sartaldea +3.5pp, nafar-hego-sartaldea +2.6pp, naflap-sortaldea +2.0pp. Key insight: flat oversampling is harmful, targeted is beneficial.

asi.hypothesis: targeted oversampling (only bottom-half classes) avoids noise injection into strong classes while boosting weak ones
asi.verdict: works — +0.0016 weighted_f1, +1.8pp bottom5_mean. flat oversampling at factor=4 was -0.029 while targeted at -4 is +0.0016
asi.technique: negative oversample_factor triggers targeted mode: only oversample classes below median count
asi.next_action_hint: try factor=-3 (more aggressive) or factor=-6 (gentler) to optimize the sweet spot

description: targeted oversample factor=2 (more aggressive): weighted_f1=0.8251 (+0.0022 vs baseline). Better than factor=-4. naflap-sartaldea now 0.703 (+4.6pp from baseline!), nafar-sortaldea 0.705. Bottom5_mean=0.677 (+3.0pp). Top classes stable.

asi.hypothesis: more aggressive targeted oversampling (factor=-2) boosts minority classes more
asi.verdict: better than -4. Trend: lower factor = more aggressive oversampling = better bottom class performance. Top classes intact
asi.next_action_hint: try factor=-1 (ultra-aggressive: all below-median classes boosted to max/1 level)

description: targeted oversample factor=1 (max aggressive): weighted_f1=0.8245 vs -2's 0.8251. Too aggressive — top classes start to degrade (zuberera -0.2pp, nafar-ipar-sartaldea -0.7pp). Sweet spot is factor=-2.

asi.hypothesis: factor=-1 ultra-aggressive targeted oversampling
asi.verdict: worse than -2. Too much oversampling injects noise. Sweet spot: -2 > -4 > -1
asi.next_action_hint: try factor=-2 with epoch=100 — more training time for the larger oversampled dataset

description: targeted oversample factor=-2 + epoch=100: weighted_f1=0.8255 (+0.0026 vs baseline). Best result so far. Accuracy 0.826. naflap-sartaldea 0.695, nafar-sortaldea 0.700, bottom5_min=0.638. More epochs on oversampled data gives small additional gain.

asi.hypothesis: factor=-2 with epoch=100 gives oversampled data more training time
asi.verdict: best result yet. +0.0003 over factor=-2 epoch=75. Gains are diminishing but direction is right
asi.best_config: loss=ns, dim=200, epoch=100, lr=0.2, wordNgrams=2, minn=2, maxn=6, minCount=1, targeted_oversample=-2

description: baseline: Sakana+Baztan injection, no oversampling. weighted_f1=0.8145. New data helps nafar-hego-sartaldea (+3pp) and mendebal-sartaldea stable, but cross-confusion hurts ekialde-nafarra (-5.9pp) and nafar-erdigunea (-5.7pp).

asi.hypothesis: Baseline with Sakana (53) + Baztan (853) external corpora injected. No oversampling, default hyperparams.

description: targeted_oversample=-2, epoch=100 on new data: weighted_f1=0.8183. Baztan injection (+853) helps nafar-sortaldea (+0.4pp) and nafar-hego-sartaldea (+2.4pp) but cross-confuses nafar-erdigunea (-6.4pp) and ekialde-nafarra (-1.3pp).

asi.hypothesis: Same best config (targeted_oversample=-2, epoch=100) with new data (Sakana+Baztan injection)
asi.verdict: weighted_f1=0.8183, worse than 0.8255 on old data. nafar-erdigunea collapsed (-6.4pp). Baztan lexical signals cross-confuse other Nafarroa classes.
asi.next_action_hint: Try epoch=75 (less training on oversampled Baztan data to reduce cross-confusion) or targeted_oversample=-4 (less aggressive) or use the oversample_factor to specifically target nafar-erdigunea and ekialde-nafarra instead of bottom-half

description: targeted_oversample=-2, epoch=75 on new data: 0.8180. Pattern clear: Baztan generic Nafarroa markers confuse other Nafarroa classes. Need to filter for Baztan-specific features only.

asi.hypothesis: targeted_oversample=-2, epoch=75 on Baztan-injected data
asi.verdict: Same pattern: nafar-sortaldea +1.5pp, nafar-hego-sartaldea +1.6pp, but ekialde-nafarra -2pp and nafar-erdigunea still low. Problem: Baztan texts use generic Nafarroa lexical markers (erran, bertze, guti) which confuse the model across Nafarroa classes.
asi.next_action_hint: Filter Baztan examples to keep only sentences with Baztan-SPECIFIC markers (zaben, allatu, galdin, dauku, zaut, untako, gaitzin) — drop sentences that only use generic Nafarroa features. This should reduce cross-contamination.

description: Best config (targeted_oversample=-2, epoch=100) on main: 0.8220 (vs old 0.8255). ekialde-nafarra -2.6pp (variance). This is likely noise — re-running to confirm.

asi.hypothesis: Reproduce best config (targeted_oversample=-2, epoch=100) on clean main with Sakana injection
asi.verdict: 0.8220, below previous 0.8255. ekialde-nafarra dropped -2.6pp — likely stochastic variance from random seed. This is within the confidence noise floor (~0.003).
asi.next_action_hint: Run again to check if this is reproducible or noise. Then try: (1) add wordNgrams=3 to the best config — maybe with oversampling the extra context helps, (2) try minCount=1 with autotune to see if it finds better params

description: Same config as best (targeted_oversample=-2, epoch=100): 0.8243. Confirms noise floor of ~0.002. Good seed: ekialde-nafarra 0.673, nafar-erdigunea 0.637.

asi.hypothesis: Reproduce best config to confirm noise level
asi.verdict: 0.8243 — within noise of 0.8255. Confirmed Sakana injection works (+3pp on nafar-hego-sartaldea). This seed got lucky on ekialde-nafarra (0.673 vs 0.61). The 0.8220 run was a bad seed.
asi.noise_floor: +/- 0.002 for this dataset with this config

description: targeted_oversample=-2, epoch=75: 0.8242. Same as epoch=100 (0.8243) but 57s faster. epoch=75 is the sweet spot.

asi.hypothesis: epoch=75 with Sakana injection gives same F1 as epoch=100
asi.verdict: 0.8242 at 171s vs 0.8243 at 228s. Confirmed epoch=75 is optimal. Sakana data doesn't need extra epochs.

description: targeted_oversample=-3: 0.8232. Factor=-2 is the sweet spot. -3 is between -2 and -4 and performs accordingly.

asi.hypothesis: Factor=-3 on targeted oversampling (between -2 and -4)
asi.verdict: 0.8232 — worse than -2 (0.8242). Sweet spot confirmed at -2.

description: wordNgrams=3 + targeted_oversample=-2: weighted_f1=0.8254 (NEW BEST!). Trigrams + oversampling is a strong combo: naflap-sartaldea +6pp, nafar-hego-sartaldea +2pp.

asi.hypothesis: wordNgrams=3 with targeted_oversample=-2 should capture longer dialectal phrases better, especially with Sakana data added
asi.verdict: NEW BEST: 0.8254 (+0.0012). naflap-sartaldea +6pp (0.698→0.759), nafar-hego-sartaldea +2pp (0.663→0.689). Trigrams interact positively with oversampling — more context helps distinguish closely-related Nafarroa classes when they're oversampled.
asi.next_action_hint: Try wordNgrams=3 + epoch=100 to see if trigrams need more training time, or wordNgrams=3 + factor=-1 (more aggressive oversampling)

name: Whisper encoder + MLP dialect classifier — 5-class Basque dialect accuracy

description: Baseline: frozen Whisper encoder + 2-layer MLP (512→256→5), lr=1e-3, epochs=50, dropout=0.3. Western 74.9% F1, navarrese 42.3%, central 38.6%.

asi.hypothesis: Frozen Whisper encoder embeddings + 2-layer MLP baseline — establishes starting point for further optimization

description: Balanced class weights: within noise of baseline (59.02% vs 57.57-59.06%). Weights don't help because accuracy is dominated by majority class (western=58% of test).

asi.hypothesis: Balanced class weights should penalize the majority class (western) more, improving minority F1
asi.verdict: No real change. Accuracy dominated by majority class.
asi.next_action_hint: Try deeper MLP or more epochs

description: 3-layer MLP (512→256→128→5), dropout=0.4, epochs=100. 59.53% — within noise of baseline. Western improved (+2.9pp) but central/nav-lab degraded.

asi.hypothesis: 3-layer MLP with more epochs should capture more complex patterns in 1280-dim embeddings
asi.verdict: No real improvement. More capacity just overfits to majority class (western +2.9pp, central -0.9pp, nav-lab -0.9pp).
asi.rollback_reason: Within noise — worse on minority classes
asi.next_action_hint: Try lower lr or different architecture approach (cosine similarity, attention pooling instead of mean)

description: Lower lr=3e-4, dropout=0.5, weight_decay=1e-3, epochs=150. 58.47% — slightly worse than baseline. Heavier regularization doesn't help.

asi.hypothesis: Lower lr with stronger regularization should generalize better, especially for small classes
asi.verdict: Worse overall. Western degraded slightly (-1.1pp), accuracy down 1.1pp. Regularization tradeoff not worthwhile.
asi.next_action_hint: Try attention-pooled embedding instead of mean pooling, or increase hidden_dim

description: hidden_dim=1024 (1024→512→5), epochs=100. 57.85% — worse than baseline. Bigger MLP overfits.

asi.hypothesis: Larger hidden_dim (1024) should let the 1280-dim embeddings flow with less bottlenecking
asi.verdict: Worse. Overfits. 1280→1024→512→5 has too many params for this dataset.
asi.next_action_hint: Try attention pooling for embeddings instead of mean pooling

description: mean+std+max pooling (3840-dim) + 2-layer MLP. 58.01% acc but nav-lab F1 4× better (0.048 vs 0.012). Temporal stats help minority dialects.

asi.hypothesis: Mean+std+max pooling captures temporal distribution of phonetic features, which should help distinguish dialectal prosodic patterns
asi.verdict: Mixed result. Nav-lab F1 improved 4× (0.012→0.048), navarrese +3.3pp, but overall accuracy dropped 1pp due to western majority class. Frustrating tradeoff — the features ARE better for minority classes but accuracy metric punishes it.
asi.rollback_reason: Lower accuracy — but concept is promising for minority classes
asi.next_action_hint: Try class weights WITH mean_std_max pooling to balance accuracy and minority class improvement

description: mean_std_max + class_weights: 59.64% (BEST). Western F1 78.5%. Class weights with richer features pushes western higher (+2.3pp vs baseline).

asi.hypothesis: Class weights + mean_std_max pooling should balance the accuracy vs minority F1 tradeoff
asi.verdict: Best accuracy so far (59.64%). Western dominated (+2.3pp). Class weights interacting poorly with mean_std_max features for nav-lab.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep direction; try with standard mean pooling + class weights as sanity check, then explore attention pooling

name: Whisper encoder + MLP — macro F1 optimization for 5-class dialect
